title: x402 isn’t good (yet) — Jan Curn, Apify
talk_summary: Jan Curn of Apify argues x402 agentic payments are still immature: the mandatory HTTP 402 conflicts with MCP's 401, the 'exact' and 'up to' schemes both allow double-spending, and metered billing forced them into charge-then-refund workarounds. Their fix was a thin agent-facing markdown endpoint (agi.apify.com) that sells prepaid tokens, decoupling fast-changing agent protocols from their stable customer API.

takeaways.technique: Agent-facing markdown endpoint decoupled from stable API
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of adding new payment endpoints or changing their customer API, they publish a single ugly markdown page at a separate hostname that instructs agents how to buy a prepaid token, which then works through the normal API/MCP.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's just a simple website with like one markdown document... there's instructions for agents like, 'Hey, how can you actually buy things on Appify yourself'

takeaways.technique: Prepaid token abstraction over volatile protocols
takeaways.what_they_do: They convert any payment scheme into a prepaid balance token, so downstream services only ever see one stable auth mechanism regardless of which payment protocol the agent used.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent comes to agent.apify.com gets basically can buy a prepaid token... then they can use the Apify token through our normal API

takeaways.technique: Assume untrusted counterparties; settle before doing expensive work
takeaways.what_they_do: They flag that x402 lets a client reuse one wallet signature across many requests (double-spend), so providers either do work before settlement (risking non-payment) or must settle first and guarantee completion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the buyer can use the same wallet and same money to other transaction... there is like nothing preventing the the client from double spending

takeaways.technique: Batch/escrow settlement for metered long jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: Coinbase's new batch settlement scheme escrows funds, issues off-chain vouchers for micro-payments, and settles on-chain in batches, avoiding per-call blockchain writes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this transactions are the basically off-chain... you don't need to like write this like to the to the to the blockchain, which again is inefficient, slow

takeaways.technique: Buy vs build economics shift when tokens are paid
takeaways.what_they_do: Curn predicts that once token subsidies end, agents will increasingly buy external services instead of building from scratch because the economics finally favor it.
